newsitem.title: USA: U.S. shares inch back down, mirroring bonds.
newsitem.headline: U.S. shares inch back down, mirroring bonds.

text.p: U.S. stocks returned to opening lows in late morning trade on Friday, suffering renewed profit-taking as the bond market continued its slide and created concern about higher higher interest rates.
The Dow Jones Industrial, which made an effort to pare its losses, could not withstand pressure from falling bond prices. For the second time in the session, it was down around 100 points at 8087.
The Nasdaq composite shed 19 points to 1605.
Declining issues outnumbered advancing issues by more than five to one on the New York Stock Exchange and by around two to one on Nasdaq.
A weak bond market sparked the broader market's fall, with the long bond losing around one full point to yield 6.60 percent.

"Stocks are taking it on the chin pretty much across the board here," Doug Myers, vice president of equity trading at Interstate/Johnson Lane, said. "I don't have anything up on my screen except for gold."
Bonds were hurt by technical and supply concerns.
